scope_line: Scope: the posthog monorepo (Django app, products/, ee/, Node CDP services, Rust services, MCP service, CI). PostHog Cloud operations and separate SDK repositories are out of scope. Many products here run PostHog's evolve loop for customers' software; see the construct note in the reading.

MAL-01.rationale: Focused application: universal entity criterion (fixed per-archetype rule). Warehouse views and group types are runtime data models, created by analysts through queries.

MAL-02.evidence: Event and person property definitions carry a validated property_type and format editable in Data management and read by queries and the UI (products/event_definitions/backend/models/property_definition.py:73-152). v0.3 moved the privacy tag to GOV-03.

MAL-03.rationale: Focused application: universal entity criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-04.rationale: Focused application: universal entity criterion (fixed per-archetype rule). The endpoints product publishes APIs from saved queries.

MAL-05.rationale: Focused application: universal entity criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-06.evidence: OpenAPI schema generated from the Django API and used to generate typed TypeScript for the frontend and MCP service (services/mcp/src/api/generated.ts); structured validation errors. No mutation dry-run, so not 4.

MAL-07.evidence: Dashboards store tile layouts as JSON per dashboard with templates (products/dashboards/backend/models); insight definitions are schema-validated queries (posthog/schema.py) edited with live preview by project members. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Only dashboards are layout-as-data; product pages are code.
MAL-07.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

MAL-08.rationale: Focused application: generic widgets from entity definitions (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-09.evidence: No UI localisation (no locale files in the tree); light and dark themes from design-system tokens (packages/quill) that tenants cannot override.
MAL-09.alt_note: Tokens are externalised in a design system, engineer-managed.

MAL-10.evidence: Actions, cohorts, feature-flag release conditions, insight alerts and CDP functions with filters are defined as data in the UI across all event and person data; functions can be test-invoked before saving (nodejs/src/cdp/cdp-api.ts:280-281).
MAL-10.alt_note: Functions are machine-readable and testable against real events; versioning and AI authoring are not verified.

MAL-11.evidence: Events feed CDP destinations with per-function logs and metrics and scheduled invocations (nodejs/src/cdp); batch exports to warehouses support backfills, which amounts to replay (products/batch_exports).
MAL-11.alt_note: Replay and per-project streams exist; event schemas are described, not generated, from definitions.

MAL-12.evidence: Hog functions run in the HogVM with a memory cap (DEFAULT_MAX_MEMORY 64 MB, common/hogvm) and a closed built-in function set, triggered by events and incoming webhooks, with per-function logs. No outbound egress guard was found in nodejs/src/cdp.
MAL-12.alt_note: If Hog's closed function set counts as an allowlist and egress control exists outside the paths searched.

GOV-01.evidence: Design system with tokens (packages/quill) and Storybook visual tests (.github/workflows/ci-storybook.yml); no automated accessibility scanning (the Playwright audit workflow audits flakes).
GOV-01.alt_note: Kit and tokens exist; the anchors bundle kit and scans.

GOV-02.evidence: Activity logging on most models with an activity page (posthog/models/activity_logging), retention by entitlement (retention.py:71), and recorded approval decisions on change requests (products/approvals/backend/models.py:112-140). Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Activity logging covers most, not all, models.
GOV-02.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

GOV-03.evidence: Data deletion requests and async deletion remove a person's data across products (posthog/api/data_deletion_request.py, posthog/models/async_deletion); not driven by field-level privacy tags.
GOV-03.alt_note: Admin-triggered erasure is generic across products; only tag-driven coverage is missing.

GOV-04.evidence: Resource-level access control and scoped API keys (products/access_control, posthog/scopes.py); semgrep and image scanning in CI on changed paths (.github/workflows/ci-security.yaml:60-174).

GOV-05.evidence: The activity log records before-and-after changes for flags, insights, dashboards and more; no general revert across customisation surfaces. The higher reading of 3 was dropped under the inventory rule (a 3 needs every default surface at 3): Revert is not available across customisation surfaces.

GOV-06.evidence: Change requests carry the intended change, a validation status and a policy snapshot, and are reviewed and then applied (products/approvals/backend/models.py:15-65); scheduled changes for flags (products/approvals/backend/scheduled_changes.py). No staging-data preview.
GOV-06.alt_note: A first-class proposal and review object exists; only preview on staging data is missing.

GOV-07.evidence: Approval policies per registered action class with conditions evaluated on the change intent, named approvers, bypass roles and recorded Approval decisions (products/approvals/backend/policies.py:37-147, actions/registry.py, models.py:112-140).

GOV-08.evidence: Customer definitions (insights, flags, functions) are data carried forward by Django migrations; no automated compatibility check or versioned extension contract was found.

ARC-01.evidence: ClickHouse event store with property materialisation driven by query analysis (ee/clickhouse/materialized_columns/analyze.py:89, columns.py:440), HogQL limits per context (posthog/hogql/constants.py:94-111) and cached query results.
ARC-01.alt_note: Query limits and materialisation from usage approach 'plans derived from definitions with cost limits'.

ARC-05.evidence: Multi-tenant organisations and projects with quota limiting and per-team throttles; no noisy-neighbour detection evidenced.
ARC-05.alt_note: Per-tenant limits are extensive; detection may exist in operations tooling outside the repository.

ARC-06.evidence: Performance suites exist (services/mcp/vitest.perf.config.mts and service benchmarks); no documented per-surface limits.

DEL-02.evidence: Independently deployable services with their own images: Django web, Node CDP and ingestion, Rust capture and flag services, and an MCP worker on Cloudflare (25 Dockerfiles; rust/, nodejs/, services/mcp/wrangler.jsonc).

DEL-03.evidence: tach enforces module boundaries and interfaces in CI (tach.toml, .github/workflows/ci-backend.yml) with isolation baselines for product modules (products/isolation_baseline.txt).

DEL-05.evidence: Backend, frontend, Rust, Playwright, Storybook, migration and semgrep checks run on pull requests with impacted-target selection from the import map (.github/scripts/tach_map.py); no accessibility check.
DEL-05.alt_note: Every class except accessibility is covered.

MAL-13.evidence: Hog function templates for sources, transformations and destinations, site apps, dashboard templates and per-product MCP tool definitions; no plugin points for PostHog's own UI, theme or text.
MAL-13.alt_note: Declarative and code extension exists for server and layout surfaces.

MAL-14.evidence: User code runs in the HogVM with memory limits and a closed function set; egress control was not evidenced.

MAL-15.evidence: Functions are test-invoked with logs and metrics before saving (nodejs/src/cdp/cdp-api.ts:280); per-PR Hogbox preview environments for PostHog's own developers (.github/workflows/hogbox-preview-env.yml).

MAL-19.evidence: MCP service typed from the generated OpenAPI schema (services/mcp/src/api/generated.ts) with tools declared per product in YAML (57 products/*/mcp/tools.yaml), scoped keys and OAuth, and MCP evals (services/mcp/evals). Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: If generation from API definitions does not count as generation from entity definitions.
MAL-19.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 4 on the evidence above.

ai.evidence: MCP service with typed tools per product and scoped keys (services/mcp).

MAL-20.evidence: PostHog AI answers members with taxonomy-grounded tools and creates insights, dashboards and other objects (ee/hogai, products/posthog_ai); offline and CI evaluation harnesses (ee/hogai/eval).
MAL-20.alt_note: An evaluation harness exists; not every UI action has a conversational equivalent.

ai.evidence: A grounded assistant that answers and creates objects (ee/hogai).

GOV-09.evidence: Scoped personal API keys and OAuth (posthog/scopes.py), approval policies on mutating actions, activity log and throttles; client idempotency identifiers on some writes only (posthog/api/data_deletion_request.py:147); no dry-run.
GOV-09.alt_note: Scoped identity, policy gates, limits and audit are present.

ai.evidence: AI acts within the user's team with access control and approval policies; idempotency only on some writes.

MAL-16.evidence: Revenue analytics maps Stripe and event-based sources onto one canonical set of revenue views (products/revenue_analytics/backend/views/sources); warehouse sources share one import framework (products/warehouse_sources). Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: The canonical model covers one domain (revenue).
MAL-16.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

MAL-17.evidence: Warehouse source definitions and CDP destination templates follow shared interfaces covering auth, sync schedules, incremental sync and delivery; admins install and configure them in the UI.

MAL-18.evidence: API paths are unversioned; incremental warehouse sync merges by primary key; no public deprecation windows.
MAL-18.alt_note: The API is documented and sync is idempotent.

EXP-01.rationale: Focused application: adjacent-domain criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

EXP-02.rationale: Focused application: adjacent-domain criterion (fixed per-archetype rule). More than 60 product modules extend the events and persons kernel.

EXP-03.rationale: Focused application: adjacent-domain criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

LRN-01.evidence: Events stream into ClickHouse within seconds and feed product features; PostHog instruments its own product with the same SDKs.
LRN-01.alt_note: Autocapture adds instrumentation automatically; whether that counts for PostHog's own evolution is the construct question.

LRN-02.evidence: Under the self rule, surveys and Signals concern customers' products and are not counted; no typed signals about PostHog's own configured definitions were found (searched products/signals, products/surveys, ee/hogai).
LRN-02.alt_note: PostHog AI may record typed feedback on its answers.

LRN-04.evidence: Under the self rule, Signals (which mines customers' products) is not counted; PostHog analyses its own query logs to decide what to materialise (ee/clickhouse/materialized_columns/analyze.py:89).
LRN-04.alt_note: If Signals run on PostHog's own product counts.

LRN-06.evidence: Query analysis recommends and applies materialised columns (ee/clickhouse/materialized_columns/analyze.py); Signals proposals target customers' repositories and are excluded under the self rule.

DEL-04.evidence: PostHog AI creates insights, dashboards and other configured objects on request (ee/hogai); Tasks agents that open pull requests in customers' repositories are excluded under the self rule.

ai.evidence: PostHog AI builds insights and dashboards on request.

LRN-09.evidence: Report metrics re-run stored queries over trailing windows to track a report's impact (products/signals/backend/report_metrics.py); experiments compare variants against control. Neither binds the applied change's version to a keep, revise or rollback decision.
LRN-09.alt_note: Experiments record baseline, metric, window and conclusion for flag-gated changes.

LRN-10.evidence: The checks that govern change are code: CI tests, serializer and schema validation, and PostHog AI's evaluation suites and prompts (ee/hogai/eval/ci/*.py, ee/hogai/chat_agent/prompts). PostHog's own team curates PostHog AI's offline evaluation datasets by hand from production traces (ee/hogai/eval/README.md, 'continuously review traces and curate your datasets'), which is level 1: improvement by people, outside the shipped product's change path. Approval policies are admin-editable data (products/approvals/backend/models.py:149-181, api.py:179-260) but are not versioned or activity-logged and are not linked to measured results. The PostHog team also measured its AI pull-request reviewer, ReviewHog, against 35 real production incidents mapped to the PRs that caused them (products/review_hog/eval/experiments/2026-09-incident-golden-set/FINAL_REPORT.md, JUDGE_RUBRIC.md): a by-hand experiment by engineers on the checks for PostHog's own code, outside the shipped product's change path and not a first-party evolution system under rule 12. Nothing in the product records a failure or wrong pass against the check that missed it or turns it into a proposed change to that check.

DEL-06.evidence: _health, livez and _readyz endpoints (posthog/urls.py:125-133); no machine-readable deployed-configuration snapshot evidenced.
DEL-06.alt_note: Instance status APIs may expose configuration.

DEL-07.evidence: Optional per-pull-request Hogbox environments restore a migrated, demo-seeded database, apply the PR's migrations, hibernate to save cost and are cleaned up (.github/workflows/hogbox-preview-env.yml, hogbox-preview-cleanup.yml).

DEL-08.evidence: Playwright journeys, Storybook visual tests and impacted-target selection that maps changed files to affected tests through tach's import map (.github/scripts/tach_map.py); features are instrumented with PostHog's own events. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Coverage across roles and devices was not verified.
DEL-08.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

LRN-07.evidence: A weekly scheduled task analyses the last week of queries and materialises hot properties without being asked (posthog/tasks/scheduled.py:927, ee/settings.py:68-73, ee/clickhouse/materialized_columns/analyze.py:89). Narrow: storage layout only. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Narrow to one area.
LRN-07.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

LRN-08.evidence: Under the v0.7 boundary this scores checks on changes the product or its AI makes to its own behaviour. PostHog AI's changes go through the same validated paths as people's: flags through the validating facade (products/feature_flags/backend/max_tools.py:340-350), insights through query-schema validation (ee/hogai/tools/upsert_dashboard/tool.py:273), and approval policies where configured. The learned change (weekly property materialisation, posthog/tasks/scheduled.py:927) applies with no check or baseline evaluation. Lower reading across the two, 1.
LRN-08.alt_note: AI-made changes alone pass automated schema validation, which is level 2.

ai.evidence: AI-made flags, insights and dashboards pass automated schema and serializer validation before they are saved (products/feature_flags/backend/max_tools.py:340-350; ee/hogai/tools/upsert_dashboard/tool.py:273), and destructive dashboard updates need confirmation (:125-139); no baseline evaluation.

ARC-02.evidence: CI runs migrations up to master, a migration risk analysis and safety tests for ClickHouse migrations (.github/workflows/ci-backend.yml:1661-2034, posthog/management/commands/analyze_migration_risk.py, test_ch_migrations_are_safe.py); async migrations carry rollback steps (posthog/async_migrations).

ARC-03.evidence: Stateless Django, Node and Rust services over shared stores; the hobby deployment is single-node (docker-compose.hobby.yml) and cloud scale-out manifests are outside this repository.
ARC-03.alt_note: The services are built to scale out.

ARC-04.evidence: Celery with Redbeat for once-only schedules (pyproject.toml:21-22) and Temporal workflows with retries (posthog/temporal); ingestion routes failures to dead-letter handling (rust/common/types/src/event.rs).

ARC-07.evidence: Prometheus metrics across services (for example services/llm-gateway/src/llm_gateway/metrics/prometheus.py); no published objectives in the repository.

ARC-08.evidence: The LLM gateway has a circuit breaker for model providers (services/llm-gateway/src/llm_gateway/circuit_breaker.py) and subscriptions auto-disable after repeated failures (ee/tasks/subscriptions/auto_disable.py); other surfaces lack breakers, so a 3 is not defensible under the inventory rule.

ai.evidence: LLM gateway circuit breaker and fallback, tested (services/llm-gateway, tests/test_circuit_breaker.py).

ARC-09.evidence: No backup command or restore path in the product. The hobby upgrade script tells operators to back up the whole installation, containers and volumes, before upgrading (bin/upgrade-hobby:44-45), and takes a pg_dumpall only during its PostgreSQL version upgrade (bin/upgrade-hobby:239-242); routine backup and restore of ClickHouse, PostgreSQL and object storage are left to the operator. Evidence corrected at the v0.7 migration; score unchanged.

DEL-01.evidence: PostHog AI takes requests in conversations stored with the page and objects in context, and has a plan mode that sets out steps before acting (ee/hogai/chat_agent/prompts/plan.py); plans carry no acceptance criteria or risk class.

DEL-09.evidence: PostHog ships its own code behind its own feature flags with percentage and cohort rollouts (products/feature_flags); definition changes and materialisations are not staged.

DEL-10.evidence: Feature flags switch code features off at runtime; there is no kill switch for AI-made or materialised changes.
DEL-10.alt_note: Flags act as a runtime kill switch for most features.

LRN-03.evidence: The app captures its own exceptions into PostHog's error tracking (frontend/src/lib/colors.ts:80, products/error_tracking); friction detection for customers' products (products/signals) is excluded under the self rule.

LRN-05.evidence: Exceptions are grouped into issues with stack traces by the error tracking product used on itself.
LRN-05.alt_note: Grouping with attached context meets level 2.

ai.evidence: Diagnosis of PostHog's own issues is not model-backed.

GOV-10.evidence: PostHog AI acts through a fixed tool set with resource-level access control, and approval policies cover registered action classes (products/approvals/backend/policies.py); materialisation has no declared blast-radius limit.

ai.evidence: A fixed tool set and approval policies; no blast-radius limit.

GOV-11.evidence: Third-party text in AI tool output is defanged and fenced as data, not instructions (ee/hogai/utils/untrusted.py); AI changes are attributed in the activity log, but source inputs are not recorded.
GOV-11.alt_note: Injection fencing is systematic for session-derived content.

ai.evidence: Session-derived content is fenced as data (ee/hogai/utils/untrusted.py).

EXP-04.evidence: No unmet-demand signals about PostHog itself beyond free-text requests.

ai.evidence: No AI involvement in this behaviour.

EXP-06.evidence: Early access features let users opt into new products and betas (products/early_access_features); no success metric or keep-or-kill record.
EXP-06.alt_note: Stage-based releases approach a cohort launch.

DEL-11.rationale: Scope fact code_release_path is false: Tasks and Stamphog act on customers' repositories (products/stamphog); no first-party lane ships PostHog code changes.

AIR-01.evidence: The LLM gateway routes across providers with Cloudflare, Modal and Bedrock fallbacks and a circuit breaker (services/llm-gateway/src/llm_gateway/baseten.py:34, circuit_breaker.py), with tests (tests/test_circuit_breaker.py).

AIR-02.evidence: Generations are marked billable for AI credits in the usage report and rate-limited (ee/hogai/llm.py:129-167, 282); credits are enforced per organisation through billing.

AIR-03.evidence: PostHog AI gets taxonomy, schema and entity context through tools over the team's live data (ee/hogai/context, tools).

AIR-04.evidence: PostHog AI acts within the user's team with resource-level access control (products/access_control) and approval policies on mutating actions; covered by tests.

AIR-05.evidence: Maintained offline and CI evaluation suites per capability with scored metrics (ee/hogai/eval/ci: funnel, retention, insight search, memory, root; eval/offline).

AIR-06.evidence: LLM evals run on pull requests labelled evals-ready (.github/workflows/ci-ai.yml:2-20); they are not automatic for every AI change and no blocking threshold was found.

AIR-07.evidence: AI generations and traces are captured in PostHog's own LLM analytics, and AI changes are attributed in the activity log (ee/hogai/llm.py, ee/hogai/llm_traces_summaries).

AIR-08.evidence: Generations, traces and user feedback on PostHog AI are recorded and summarised (ee/hogai/llm_traces_summaries, chat_agent/slash_commands/commands/feedback); no drift alerts found.
AIR-08.alt_note: LLM analytics dashboards per model may act as continuous monitoring.

limits: Repository evidence only, master at the tip named above. The repository is very large (about 55,000 files); only the areas cited were read, so some capabilities are likely under-scored (for example versioning and rollback). Cloud operations, dogfooding practice and incident history are invisible here. Egress controls for Hog functions were searched for and not found; they may exist in infrastructure code outside the paths read. Single rater. Under the v0.3 self rule, Signals, Tasks and experiments on customers' products are excluded from scoring.
reading: **SAL 1.** Request → Release reaches L2: PostHog AI plans before acting and builds insights and dashboards (DEL-01 2, DEL-04 2). Issue → Fix stops at L1 because nothing diagnoses PostHog's own issues (LRN-05 1); its Signals product does this for customers' products and is excluded under the self rule. **Strengths:** migration risk analysis in CI (ARC-02 3), Temporal and Celery work (ARC-04 3), and feature flags on its own code (DEL-09 2). **Blocks L3:** no backup in the repository (ARC-09 1), and definition rollback covers only some surfaces (GOV-05 2).

persistent_data.evidence: Events in ClickHouse, configuration in PostgreSQL, recordings in object storage.

schema_changes.evidence: Django and ClickHouse migrations, plus property materialisation that adds columns at runtime (ee/clickhouse/materialized_columns/columns.py).

multi_tenant.evidence: Organisations and projects with their own members, roles and access control share one deployment, with quotas (products/access_control); these are separately administered groups, not one person's workspaces.

hosted_service.evidence: Django web, Celery and Temporal workers, Node ingestion and Rust capture services.

machine_actions.evidence: The API with scoped personal keys and an MCP server change PostHog objects (posthog/scopes.py, services/mcp).

agent_mutations.evidence: PostHog AI creates and edits insights, dashboards, feature flags, experiments and surveys (ee/hogai/tools, products/*/backend/max_tools.py).

evolution_auto_apply.evidence: PostHog AI changes are made on request in a conversation; weekly property materialisation applies without approval (posthog/tasks/scheduled.py:927), but it is scheduled maintenance, not a change from the evolution loop.

definition_change_path.evidence: Insights, dashboards, feature flags, actions and approval policies are definitions.

code_release_path.evidence: False under the v0.7 definition. PostHog AI drafts Hog transformation code into the editor (products/cdp/backend/max_tools.py:51), but a person saves and enables it and it is versioned and restored with the function definition (products/cdp/backend/api/hog_function.py:1677); the AI does not activate code. Tasks and Stamphog act on repositories (products/stamphog); no first-party lane ships PostHog's own code changes.

ai_features.evidence: PostHog AI (ee/hogai) and the LLM gateway (services/llm-gateway).

ai_data_access.evidence: PostHog AI queries the team's events, insights and taxonomy (ee/hogai/context).

ai_actions.evidence: PostHog AI creates and edits insights, dashboards and other objects (ee/hogai/tools).

change_kinds.name: Charts, reports and dashboards
change_kinds.who: product and growth teams in a project
change_kinds.evidence: Members build insights and dashboards in the UI with live preview; PostHog AI drafts them on request (ee/hogai/tools/create_insight.py; ee/hogai/tools/upsert_dashboard/tool.py:116, with a confirmation preview for updates that remove insights at :125-139) and the member keeps or edits the result. Undo: a deleted dashboard and its tiles are restored through undo-delete (products/dashboards/backend/api/dashboard.py:2424, :2747; posthog/api/file_system/deletion.py), and edits are recorded in the activity log with before and after values; there is no one-step revert to an earlier version of a dashboard or insight, so undoing an edit means editing it back from the logged values. Reach 2 rests on DEL-04 2.

change_kinds.name: Who sees which feature (feature flags)
change_kinds.who: engineers and product managers in a project
change_kinds.evidence: Flags are created and edited in the UI and API with validated release conditions; PostHog AI creates flags on request through the same validated facade (products/feature_flags/backend/max_tools.py:211, create_flag with validation errors returned at :340-350). Undo: switch the flag off, restore a deleted or archived flag, and read any earlier version reconstructed from history (products/feature_flags/backend/version_history.py; versions endpoint api/feature_flag.py:4780); restoring an earlier version is done by editing it back, not by a revert button. Approval policies can require a reviewer for flag changes (products/approvals/backend/policies.py).

change_kinds.name: A/B tests and experiments
change_kinds.evidence: Experiments are set up and launched in the UI; PostHog AI creates them in draft for a person to configure and launch (products/experiments/backend/max_tools.py:97, :158). Undo: reset an experiment to draft or archive it (products/experiments/backend/experiment_service.py:1963, :2996).

change_kinds.name: Where data is sent and how it is transformed
change_kinds.evidence: Destinations, transformations and sources are configured from templates in the UI and test-invoked before saving (nodejs/src/cdp/cdp-api.ts:280); PostHog AI drafts transformation code, filters and inputs into the editor for a person to save (products/cdp/backend/max_tools.py:51, :153, :236). Undo: every live change is a numbered revision that can be restored (products/cdp/backend/api/hog_function.py:1395-1414, revisions restore at :1677-1708).

change_kinds.name: Surveys shown to users
change_kinds.evidence: Surveys are built and launched in the UI; PostHog AI drafts a survey and launches it only with explicit confirmation (products/surveys/backend/max_tools.py:291-305, is_dangerous_operation at :298). Undo: stop a survey by ending it or archive it (end_date and archived fields, products/surveys/backend/api/survey.py:939-940); edits have no version history.

change_kinds.name: New kinds of analysis and changes to PostHog's own screens
change_kinds.evidence: New analysis types, product screens and behaviour are PostHog code in this monorepo, changed by pull request and release; no first-party lane builds PostHog's own code from users' requests (code_release_path false; Tasks and Stamphog act on repositories, not on a running PostHog). Engineers only.

ai_delivery.evidence: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, AI_POLICY.md, .agents/skills, .claude (agents, commands, hooks, skills), .codex, .cursorrules; agent workflows in CI: pr-autoresolve-conflicts.yml runs openai/codex-action pinned by SHA to resolve merge conflicts (manual dispatch only), review-hog.yml triggers an AI review service on labelled PRs, and stamphog[bot] posts AI approvals on this repository's PRs (products/stamphog/README.md).
ai_delivery.note: AI-assisted engineering, not PostHog evolving itself. It does not meet rule 12: the agent workflows review, approve or resolve conflicts on PRs that people write; no agent lane builds PostHog changes from its users' requests or issues, and whether Stamphog approvals are required checks is set in branch protection outside the repository.

request.searched: Repository at the pinned commit: CHANGELOG.md (points to the public changelog of engineering releases), activity-log and change-request models, .github workflows. No operating records of real changes going through PostHog's own Request → Release loop in a deployment are in the repository.

fix.searched: Repository at the pinned commit: CHANGELOG.md (points to the public changelog of engineering releases), activity-log and change-request models, .github workflows. No operating records of real changes going through PostHog's own Issue → Fix loop in a deployment are in the repository.

expansion.searched: Repository at the pinned commit: CHANGELOG.md (points to the public changelog of engineering releases), activity-log and change-request models, .github workflows. No operating records of real changes going through PostHog's own Opportunity → Expansion loop in a deployment are in the repository.

confidence_note: Confidence for criteria whose score did not change in the v0.7 migration was assigned at migration from the recorded evidence; confidence for new and changed readings (kinds of change, LRN-10 and every re-read criterion) comes from re-reading the source at the pinned commit.
